newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian dies in anti-Miss World human torch protest.
newsitem.headline: Indian dies in anti-Miss World human torch protest.

text.p: A 24-year-old Indian man died after setting himself ablaze in a human torch protest against the Miss World beauty contest being staged in India, the United News of India (UNI) news agency said on Thursday.

The agency said Suresh Kumar, a tailor, shouted anti-pageant slogans as he set fire to himself at a bus stand in the heart of the southern city of Madurai, some 432 kilometres south of Bangalore where Miss World will be crowned on November 23.
Eye-witnesses said Kumar doused himself with chemicals and was engulfed in flames within seconds, leaving hundreds of bystanders powerless to help him, according to local news reports.
He was taken to hospital with burns to 90 percent of his body. Kumar died from his injuries in hospital, the reports said.
UNI said Kumar was a member of the extremist Marxist-led Democratic Youth Federation of India, and sources in Madurai added that he was unemployed.

The pageant has attracted vehement protests since one of India's most popular film stars, Amitabh Bachchan, whose company holds the rights to stage this year's contest, announced the event would be held in India for the first time in its 45-year history.
More than 20 groups have come out in protest against the pageant, decrying it as defamatory to women and an affront to Indian culture.
A women's organisation, the Mahila Jagran Samiti (Forum for Awakening Women), had already threatened that its members would commit suicide by self-immolation in protest against the show.
And local members of parliament for the Bharatiya Janata Party have said they will lay siege to Chinnaswamy cricket stadium where the crowning ceremony will take place.
A spokesman for Clea Public relations, representing the contest organisers said: "We have no comment to make on the tragedy. Our hearts reach out to the young man who has died."
The furore had already forced the Miss World organisers to hold the swimsuit parade outside India earlier this month, in the Seychelle Islands in the Indian Ocean.
The 89 contestants arrived in Bangalore in the early hours of Tuesday morning, amid a massive security operation.

Bangalore police have detained 40 people as a preventive measure against potential trouble, and have issued orders that rallies or demonstrations of more than 10 people will be unlawful until the Miss World show has quit the city on November 24.
